chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) shaving [the hair] from his Umrah [state], and taking [cutting] from the sides of all his hair upon the comb. Then he gestured to his moustache, so the barber took from it. Then he gestured towards the sides of his beard, so he took from it, then he arose.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam do to his hair and beard after finishing Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* provides a precise visual account of Imam al-Rida’s (AS) post-Ihram grooming, illustrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on following the Imams' practical examples (*sunan*) in ritual purification. It highlights the permissibility of trimming facial hair and nails immediately after exiting the sacred state, reinforcing the concept that cleanliness is an integral part of completing the pilgrimage rites. The narration serves as a primary evidence for the fiqh of *Tumatto* (shortening hair/nails) and underscores the continuity between ritual sacrifice and personal hygiene in Shia jurisprudence.
